scenes.heading: NoSQL
scenes.subheading: Flexible databases beyond the relational model
scenes.narration: NoSQL databases store data without a rigid relational schema, trading strict structure for flexibility and horizontal scale.

scenes.heading: Why NoSQL exists
bullets: Comes in document, key-value, column, and graph types
scenes.narration: NoSQL exists to handle flexible or rapidly evolving schemas that relational tables resist. It scales horizontally across many servers, which suits huge, distributed workloads. Each type is optimized for a specific access pattern rather than general querying. And it comes in several families, including document, key-value, wide-column, and graph databases.

scenes.heading: RDBMS vs NoSQL
scenes.narration: An RDBMS enforces a fixed schema and strong consistency, and typically scales by adding power to one machine. NoSQL embraces flexible schemas and often accepts eventual consistency in exchange for scaling out across many machines. The right choice depends on whether you value strict structure or massive, flexible scale.

scenes.heading: Picking a NoSQL type
scenes.narration: Choosing NoSQL starts with understanding how your application reads and writes data. You match that access pattern to the shape of your data. Then you pick the NoSQL family that fits and model your data specifically for that pattern.

scenes.text: NoSQL trades rigid schemas and strict consistency for flexibility and horizontal scale.
scenes.narration: The heart of NoSQL is trading rigid schemas and strict consistency for the flexibility and horizontal scale that many modern applications demand.
